messages.content: Now that we have settled on Amelia Island, compare the three hotels on the full six-night cost, not the headline rate. I also want the actual walk to the sand and the cancellation terms. We should finish with two choices, but do not book either one.

I’ll compare Omni Amelia Island Resort, SpringHill Suites Amelia Island, and Hampton Inn Amelia Island at Fernandina Beach for September 12 through 18, one room for two adults. Before I price room categories, should I look for one queen bed, a king, or two separate beds?
Morgan and I are sharing the room, so start with a queen bed. A king is fine when it is the larger alternative; we do not need separate beds.

Understood. I’ll use a queen room where available and accept a king category when that is the comparable larger-bed option. I’ll keep taxes, mandatory property charges, and parking visible as separate lines.
Good. Start with the totals. The nightly numbers I saw were all misleadingly close.

For refundable rates currently showing for all six nights, the comparison is: SpringHill Suites, queen studio suite, $1,746 room charge, $209.52 estimated lodging tax, and $90 parking, totaling $2,045.52. Hampton Inn, one-queen room, $1,554 room charge and $186.48 tax, with breakfast and self-parking included, totaling $1,740.48. Omni, resort-view king room, $2,514 room charge, $301.68 tax, $240 resort fee, and $240 self-parking, totaling $3,295.68. None of these totals includes optional food or valet service.
That makes the Omni gap much bigger than it looked. Is the resort fee already taxed in your figure, or could another charge appear at checkout?

The displayed Omni tax estimate applies to the quoted room and mandatory resort charge as presented in the checkout breakdown. The $3,295.68 total also includes six nights of self-parking. Valet parking, incidentals, and any optional activities would be extra, but I do not see another mandatory destination charge in this quote.
Now describe the beach route precisely. “Near the beach” is not useful if we have to cross a highway or wander through another property.

Omni is the only true beachfront option: guests follow the resort’s interior path east from the pool area to its beach boardwalk, without crossing a public road. The route is roughly 500 to 900 feet depending on the building assignment. SpringHill is across Atlantic Avenue from Main Beach Park. From the lobby, use the marked crossing at Atlantic Avenue, continue on the park walkway, and enter the beach on the public boardwalk beside the Main Beach facilities. It is about 0.2 mile and normally four to five minutes. Atlantic Avenue is a local beach road there, though it can be busier around park events.
And the Hampton? That is the one I am least clear about.

Hampton is inland on Sadler Road. The direct public route runs east on the Sadler Road sidewalk, crosses the side-street entrances near the beach businesses, then reaches Seaside Park at the end of Sadler. The public beach entrance is the Seaside Park boardwalk. The mapped walk is about 0.4 mile, generally eight to ten minutes. There is no need to enter another hotel, but the final approach has more driveway crossings and traffic than the SpringHill route.
So SpringHill is across one road at a marked crossing, while Hampton is several blocks with multiple driveways. Is that a fair distinction?

Yes. SpringHill has one principal road crossing and then a direct park walkway. Hampton remains a legitimate walk to a public entrance, but it is longer and less pleasant because of the commercial driveways along Sadler Road. Omni avoids a public-road crossing altogether.
Check whether the SpringHill route is usable early in the morning. I do not want the beach access tied to park office hours.

The Main Beach boardwalk is an outdoor public access route rather than an indoor facility, so the route does not depend on a park office being open. Posted beach or park restrictions would still apply, and temporary closures are possible, but normal early-morning pedestrian access does not require passing through a locked building or hotel-controlled gate.
Now give me the refund deadlines and the actual penalty after each deadline.

SpringHill’s quoted flexible rate permits cancellation without charge through 11:59 p.m. local hotel time on September 10; after that, the stated penalty is one night plus tax, estimated at $325.92. Hampton permits free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. local time on September 11; the late-cancellation or no-show penalty is one night plus tax, estimated at $290.08. Omni’s refundable offer is cancellable through 5:00 p.m. local time on September 5; after that, the quoted penalty is a two-night deposit including applicable tax and resort charges, estimated at $1,018.56.
The Omni deadline is much earlier, but it is still refundable long enough for us to make a deliberate decision. Are these all pay-later rates rather than prepaid rates?

SpringHill and Hampton are shown as flexible pay-at-property rates with a card guarantee. Omni is not fully prepaid, but it requires a two-night deposit when the reservation is made; that deposit is refundable if cancellation occurs before the September 5 deadline. The remaining Omni balance is due under the resort’s arrival terms.
Drop Hampton. The savings over SpringHill are only about $305, and the longer roadside walk is not worth it for six days. Keep SpringHill as the practical choice and Omni as the splurge.

That leaves a clear pair. SpringHill is $2,045.52 complete, with a marked crossing to the Main Beach public boardwalk and free cancellation through September 10. Omni is $3,295.68 complete, with an on-property beach boardwalk and free cancellation through September 5, subject to its refundable two-night deposit. The difference is $1,250.16 for the six-night stay.
Before we stop, make sure the room descriptions do not quietly promise an ocean view. We are comparing access right now, not paying more for a view.

Correct. The SpringHill quote is for a queen studio suite without a guaranteed ocean view, and the Omni quote is for a resort-view king room. Neither total assumes an ocean-view upgrade. At Omni, building placement can also change the walk within the property, but every quoted room uses the resort’s beach access rather than a public-road crossing.
That is enough. Leave both unbooked and record the exact totals, routes, and deadlines so we can decide later.

Both options remain unbooked for September 12 through 18. SpringHill Suites Amelia Island: queen studio suite, $2,045.52 total, approximately 0.2 mile via the marked Atlantic Avenue crossing and Main Beach public boardwalk, free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. local time September 10, then an estimated $325.92 penalty. Omni Amelia Island Resort: resort-view king room, $3,295.68 total including resort fee and self-parking, on-property path to the resort beach boardwalk with no public-road crossing, free cancellation through 5:00 p.m. local time September 5, then an estimated $1,018.56 penalty. The refundable Omni rate requires a two-night deposit. Hampton has been removed from consideration, and no reservation was made.

For their September 12-18 Amelia Island trip, SpringHill Suites and Omni Amelia Island Resort are the two finalists and remain unbooked. Their cancellation deadlines are September 10 and September 5 respectively, and the Omni quote requires a refundable two-night deposit. Hampton Inn was removed from consideration. The January 12-15 New Orleans trip and Cambria Hotel remain confirmed, Midtown Lodge Raleigh remains booked, and registrar approval is still pending for the proposed Boston hotel replacement. Other confirmed arrangements remain unchanged.
